raw_case_text:
A 64-year-old male patient, resident of Vadodara city, Gujarat state located in the western India, who is a known case of diabetes mellitus II, hypothyroidism, and ocular myasthenia gravis since 3 years presented to our tertiary care hospital named Sheth VS General hospital located in Ahmedabad city (Gujarat state) with 8 days history of acute fever, malaise, generalized rash, and multiple joint pains. He complained of an acute onset of sensorimotor quadriparesis and urinary retention since 7 days which was followed 1 day later by H/O altered sensorium. He had no history of headache, vomiting, seizure, dimness of vision, double vision, dysphagia, change in voice, and neck/back pain. The patient had already received methyl prednisolone injection pulse therapy 1 g each for 5 days before presenting to our institute to which he responded partially in form of improved level of consciousness. The patient had no recent history of travelling outside the state of Gujarat or India.
The patient was conscious oriented following verbal command and had no neck rigidity. Cranial nerves: left eye ptosis+; no facial/neck flexor weakness; and mixed dysarthria+.
Nutrition-no undue wasting or hypertrophy; tone: spastic both upper limbs (UL) with flaccid both lower limbs; power (according to the MRC scale): 4/5 in both UL and 1/5 in both LL; with B/L hand grip weakness and B/L dorsiflexor weakness;
Deep tendon reflexes (DTRs) were +3 in both UL with B/L pectoralis reflex and jaw jerk+; DTRs were absent in both lower limbs (LL), and planters were absent.
Impaired joint, position, and vibration sensations up to metatarsophalangeal joints in both the lower limbs and up to metacarpophalangeal joints in both the upper limbs were noted with normal cerebellar examination.
Including complete blood count, random blood sugar, renal and liver function tests, and serum electrolytes were within normal limits except for slightly raised WBC to 14500/microL, CRP 16, and CPK total 84. Serum CHIKV IgM detection by ELISA came positive. Serum chikungunya real-time PCR, which is a qualitative test of chikungunya RNA by a standard procedure, was positive. RNA was extracted using the QIAamp Viral RNA Mini kit (Qiagen). One-step RT-PCR was performed using the access quick RT-PCR kit (Promega), in accordance with the manufacturer's protocol, employing primer pairs targeting the E1 gene designed from the nucleotide sequence of the reference S27 strain (GenBank accession number AF490259; CK 13, TTA CAT CAC GTG CGA TA C; CK-14, CTT TC TCT CAG GG TGC GAC TTT). The amplification was performed in a 50 microL total reaction volume with the Promega Access Quick One-Step RT-PCR kit, 50 pmol of each forward and reverse primer, and 2 microL of extracted viral RNA, in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions.
Electroencephalogram (EEG) showed generalized bilaterally symmetrical diffuse theta-delta slowing suggestive of diffuse encephalopathy. His electrophysiology study showed distal symmetrical sensory motor axonal polyneuropathy more in the lower limbs than the upper limbs. CSF routine micro: protein, 96 mg/dL, glucose, 60 mg/dL, and total cells, 140 with lymphocytic pleocytosis with negative Gram and ZN stain. CSF viral panel done by PCR was negative for neurotropic viruses. This included pan-flavivirus RNA, pan-enterovirus RNA, pan-paramyxovirus RNA detection and pan-herpes DNA detection. Patient's sample was positive for ANA (antinuclear antibody) by immunofluorescence with a dilution of 1 : 100 and 1 : 200, a homogeneous pattern, and +1 intensity. On further workup, ANA profile by immunoDOT was negative. Anti-aquaporin-4 Ab became negative. Serum and CSF investigations are depicted in Tables 1 and 2.
Multiple tiny altered signal intensity foci with restricted diffusion seen in subcortical and periventricular white matter of bilateral (B/L) cerebral hemispheres, corpus callosum, and b/L corona radiata with normal MR angiogram are shown in Figure 1. Axial T2W sagittal section showing D7 intramedullary hyperintensity is shown in Figure 2. Patchy areas of T2W hyperintensity in the cervicodorsal cord predominantly from the C7 to D9 level without significant postcontrast enhancement are shown in Figure 3. These findings were consistent with features of encephalomyelitis.
Our patient was managed with IV immunoglobulin (IgG) in a total dose of 140 grams as well as supportive treatment for his comorbidities. He was discharged in a stable hemodynamic condition with power 5/5 in both the UL and 3/5 in both the LL. The patient was advised supportive treatment and neurorehabilitation in form of active physiotherapy.
The patient responded well; his power improved; he was able to walk with one stick support with a normal bladder function with a current modified Rankin scale (mRS) of 4. No radiological investigations were done in follow-up.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 64-year-old male presented with an 8-day history of acute fever, malaise, generalized rash, and polyarthralgia, followed by a 7-day history of acute sensorimotor quadriparesis and urinary retention and a 6-day history of altered sensorium.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient developed acute fever, malaise, generalized rash, and multiple joint pains 8 days prior to admission to Sheth VS General Hospital in Ahmedabad, India. One day after fever onset (7 days prior to presentation), he developed acute-onset sensorimotor quadriparesis and urinary retention, followed 1 day later by altered sensorium. Prior to transfer, he received a 5-day course of intravenous methylprednisolone pulse therapy (1 g/day) at an outside facility, with partial improvement in his level of consciousness.
subjective.past_medical_history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypothyroidism, and ocular myasthenia gravis for 3 years. Resident of Vadodara, Gujarat, India, with no recent travel outside Gujarat or India. Received 5 days of IV methylprednisolone (1 g/day) prior to admission.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for fever, malaise, generalized rash, polyarthralgia, four-limb weakness and numbness, urinary retention, and altered sensorium (partially improved); negative for headache, vomiting, seizures, visual dimming, diplopia, dysphagia, dysphonia, or neck/back pain.

objective.physical_examination: Conscious, oriented, following verbal commands, with no neck rigidity and normal nutritional status (no muscle wasting or hypertrophy). Cranial nerves: left eye ptosis and mixed dysarthria; no facial or neck flexor weakness. Motor exam: spastic tone in bilateral upper limbs (UL) and flaccid tone in bilateral lower limbs (LL); MRC muscle power 4/5 in bilateral UL and 1/5 in bilateral LL, with bilateral hand grip and ankle dorsiflexor weakness. Reflexes: deep tendon reflexes (DTRs) hyperactive (+3) in bilateral UL with positive bilateral pectoralis reflex and brisk jaw jerk; DTRs absent in bilateral LL with absent plantar responses. Sensory and coordination: impaired joint position and vibration sense up to the MCP joints in bilateral UL and up to the MTP joints in bilateral LL; cerebellar examination normal.
objective.routine_investigations: Complete blood count, random blood glucose, renal and liver function tests, and serum electrolytes: within normal limits except for mildly elevated WBC count of 14,500/uL, C-reactive protein (CRP) 16, and total creatine phosphokinase (CPK) 84.
objective.advanced_workup: Electroencephalogram (EEG): generalized bilaterally symmetrical diffuse theta-delta slowing indicative of diffuse encephalopathy. Nerve conduction / electrophysiology studies: distal symmetrical sensorimotor axonal polyneuropathy affecting lower limbs more than upper limbs. Lumbar puncture / CSF analysis: total cells 140/uL with lymphocytic pleocytosis, protein 96 mg/dL, glucose 60 mg/dL, negative Gram and Ziehl-Neelsen (ZN) stains; CSF viral PCR panel negative for pan-flavivirus RNA, pan-enterovirus RNA, pan-paramyxovirus RNA, and pan-herpesvirus DNA. Autoimmune panel: serum ANA weakly positive by immunofluorescence (1:100 and 1:200 dilution, homogeneous pattern, +1 intensity), ANA profile by immunoDOT negative, and anti-aquaporin-4 (AQP4) antibody negative. Brain and spine MRI with MR angiogram: multiple tiny foci of altered signal intensity with restricted diffusion in bilateral subcortical and periventricular white matter, corpus callosum, and bilateral corona radiata with a normal MR angiogram; spinal MRI showed patchy T2-weighted intramedullary hyperintensities in the cervicodorsal spinal cord from C7 to D9 (prominent at D7) without significant post-contrast enhancement.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Acute chikungunya virus-associated encephalomyelitis and distal symmetrical sensorimotor axonal polyneuropathy (myeloradiculoneuropathy). Other neurotropic viral infections (flaviviruses, enteroviruses, paramyxoviruses, herpesviruses) and neuromyelitis optica (anti-AQP4) were ruled out. Confirmation: Positive serum CHIKV IgM ELISA and positive serum real-time RT-PCR targeting the CHIKV E1 gene, supported by brain/cervicodorsal spine MRI, EEG, nerve conduction studies, and CSF lymphocytic pleocytosis. Management and outcome: Treated with intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG, total dose 140 g) following prior 5-day IV methylprednisolone pulse therapy, alongside supportive management of comorbidities and active physiotherapy. Discharged hemodynamically stable with improved limb power (5/5 in bilateral UL, 3/5 in bilateral LL); on follow-up, he regained normal bladder function and ambulated with a single-stick support (modified Rankin Scale score of 4).
